verdicts.reason: A has the CTA pushed into the top-left corner next to the logo, one oversized can in the middle and two thumbnail cans abandoned in the bottom-left corner. Flavour names are stacked and cut off from their descriptors, which are listed in a different order, and the delivery line sits above the descriptors. B keeps a top-down order and puts the CTA at the bottom, but the headline breaks badly ('light' is left alone on the second line). Its text block is crammed against the logo, it has the same mismatched name/descriptor lists, and it shows one big can over two tiny ones instead of three equal products.

A has a sensible top-down flow (logo, cans, two-line headline, copy, bottom CTA). However, the three cans are drawn at inconsistent sizes and the right one is tiny. The flavour names are stacked away from their descriptors, which run in the reverse order ('Bright & zesty' sits under the Honey Rosemary position), so the product-to-description grouping is lost. B is the broken layout: the CTA is jammed top-left beside the logo, one huge can sits in the middle, two tiny cans are stranded in the bottom-left corner, and there is a dead band at the bottom.

A reads top to bottom (logo, headline, copy block, cans, CTA) with a clean headline break. Its flaws are a dense, cramped stack of type under the headline, flavour names cut off from their descriptors and listed in mismatched order, and three cans at unequal sizes with the right one shrunk and off-axis. B has the same broken layout seen elsewhere: the CTA sits in the top corner, competing with the logo, one oversized can dominates, and two thumbnail cans are left in the bottom-left corner.
